2. [RARC.5.6.3] Samples both clocks, as the engine does whenever it consumes
   an input ([LTIM.2.8.4]), whatever `clock_ns` the event carries. A pump, at
   its entry and before anything fires, then retracts the expired `ttl` facts,
   a fact being expired when its deadline is at or before the monotonic sample
   ([RARC.5.2.4]). An assert, a retract or a clock move retracts nothing: an
   expired fact stays in working memory until the next pump.

idris.name: iret_19_5__tick_clocked
idris.note: The clock takes the tick's sample (a `Tick` carries the source's monotonic sample, as in Rete/TtlSweep.idr), every fact whose deadline is at or before it is retracted, then the re-time [IRET.19.5] names. Partial for WHERE: this engine does all three as the tick is consumed, where the clause samples at the input and sweeps at the pump's entry, a clock move retracting nothing. The same state once the pump runs after the tick; between the two, an expired fact the clause keeps is gone here.

idris.name: iret_19_5__tick_clocked_view
idris.note: The clause's step, followed by the re-time, keeps the view.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__quiet_tick_clocked
idris.note: When nothing has expired and no verdict moves, the clause's step leaves the deadline table, working memory and the chains as they were and moves the clock.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__quiet_tick_is_retime
idris.note: A tick whose sweep finds nothing expired is, with the clock moved, the re-time alone.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__first_tick_moves_the_clock
idris.note: The clock takes the tick's sample: a tick sampled at 1, with the clock at 0, moves the clock to 1, computed.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__prepare_clocked
idris.note: A tick advances and sweeps and re-times; a data event, carrying no clock in this model, is swept for and applied. Partial for the sweep's placement: the clause sweeps at the pump's entry and an input retracts nothing (RARC.7.15), where this model sweeps as the input is consumed -- one state once the pump runs after a tick, a different order inside the boundary after a data event.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__sweep_net_view
idris.note: The clause's retraction of expired facts keeps the view, retracting in [LDTL.6.1]'s order and cascading.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_3__tick_then_pump_is_clocked
idris.note: The sweep at the tick, then the re-time and the run: Rete/NetworkClocked.idr's pump at the tick, where the sweep is placed the same way.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__tick_timed
idris.note: The monotonic sample, taken; the sweep at the tick, as Rete/NetworkTtl.idr's prepare has it. LESS than the clause: the clause sweeps at the pump's entry, the model at the tick; the two coincide at every pump boundary the Idris model compares.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__tick_timed_projects
idris.note: The sweep is Rete/NetworkTtl.idr's, by projection.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__quiet_tick_net
idris.note: A TICK THAT EXPIRES NOTHING MOVES ONLY THE CLOCK, on the network: working memory, terminals with their `fired` flags, dependency table and deadline table unchanged, so no activation is created, ended or re-armed by it. That is this clause's 'cycling the tick is not a change to the LHS' for the tests this engine has, which are predicates of facts: the clause's observable is a `now()` gate, which they do not read. On the one engine with both kinds of test, Rete/NetworkClocked.idr's `ldet_5_8__quiet_tick_clocked` is the statement, and Rete/NetworkTick.idr's `ldet_5_8__tick_keeps_activation` and `ldet_5_8__late_fires_once` carry the observable, on the flag reading.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__advance_net
idris.note: The advance, sharing Rete/TtlSweep.idr's choice of clock (`rarc_5_6_3__next_clock`).

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__prepare_net
idris.note: The loop's steps before firing on the network, in Rete/TtlSweep.idr's order: advance and sweep, or sweep and apply. Partial as `rarc_5_6_3__prepare` is: the clause sweeps at the pump's entry, not as an input is consumed. The agreement with FireLoop (`rlow_4_2_1__prepare_agree`) is between two models that place the sweep alike.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__sweep_net
idris.note: THE SWEEP ON THE NETWORK: every live fact whose deadline is at or before the clock retracted one at a time through alpha dispatch -- [IRET.19.3] step 2, `ds_rete_wm_retract` per fact -- in [LDTL.6.1]'s order, then the cascade.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__prepare_agree
idris.note: THE LOOP'S STEPS BEFORE FIRING AGREE: a tick advances both clocks alike and sweeps alike; a data event is swept for and applied alike.

idris.name: iret_19_5__tick_clocked_wall
idris.note: The clause's advance and sweep read no time-dependent test; the composed tick at two wall samples is one state.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__next_clock_lte
idris.note: The clock after the step is at or above the clock before it: the sample a conforming source gives never runs back ([LTIM.2.8.2]).

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__advance
idris.note: The clause's first half: the clock takes the tick's sample. A `Tick t` is the monotonic sample the source gave when the input was consumed, whatever `clock_ns` the event carried; `next_clock`'s guard against a value below the clock is one a conforming source never reaches ([LTIM.2.8.2]).

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__advance_lte
idris.note: The advance never turns the clock back.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__clock_monotone
idris.note: THE CLOCK NEVER RUNS BACKWARDS: across a boundary -- the input, the sweep, the pump -- it only advances.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__next_clock
idris.note: The clock the advance moves to: the tick's sample, guarded structurally against a sample below the clock, which [LTIM.2.8.2] rules out of any conforming source. Named so that Rete/NetworkTtl.idr's advance is the same function.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__prepare
idris.note: The loop's steps before firing, in this model's order: advance the clock if the input is a tick, sweep, apply the data event if any. The clause (RARC.7.15) samples at the input and sweeps at the PUMP'S ENTRY, an assert, a retract or a clock move retracting nothing. On a tick the two reach one state once the pump runs; on a data event the clause applies before it sweeps and this model sweeps before it applies, so a match the clause makes against an expired fact and ends at the pump never exists here. No theorem relates the two orders; the Idris model compares at pump boundaries alone, where they coincide. Partial for the placement.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__prepare_inv
idris.note: The steps before firing keep the invariant and never turn the clock back.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__sweep
idris.note: The clause's sweep: retract every `ttl` fact whose deadline is at or before the monotonic sample, propagate, cascade. What it does is the clause's; where it runs is `rarc_5_6_3__prepare`'s and that tie's `partial`.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__sweep_here_inv
idris.note: Sweeping at the current clock keeps the invariant.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__sweep_inv
idris.note: The sweep keeps the invariant, and re-establishes that every live deadline is in the future, whatever the clock was set to: this is what lets the clock advance.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_3__tick_inv
idris.note: Advancing then sweeping keeps the invariant: the advance touches only the clock, and the sweep restores the future-deadline part at the new clock.
